title: Bearings and Oblique Triangles Practice
description: Practice reading bearings, finding back bearings, and translating navigation descriptions into triangle diagrams.

questions.question: How is a standard bearing measured?
questions.explanation: A standard bearing is measured clockwise from north and is usually written with three digits.

questions.question: Which direction matches a bearing of 090°?
questions.explanation: A 090° clockwise turn from north points east.

questions.question: A bearing of 135° lies in which quadrant?
questions.explanation: 135° is between 090° and 180°, so the direction is southeast.

questions.question: From the same point, two paths have bearings 040° and 115°. What is the angle between the paths? Give the answer in degrees.
questions.explanation: Subtract the bearings because both paths start from the same point: 115° - 040° = 75°.

questions.question: From A to B, the bearing is 070°. What is the bearing from B back to A?
questions.explanation: The opposite direction is 180° away, so 070° + 180° = 250°.

questions.question: A new north line should be drawn at each new point where a bearing is measured.
questions.explanation: Each bearing is measured from north at its own location, so drawing a local north line helps keep the diagram accurate.

questions.question: From point P, point Q is 8 km away on a bearing of 025° and point R is 12 km away on a bearing of 100°. What triangle information is known for △PQR?
questions.explanation: The two known distances are sides from P, and the angle between them is 100° - 025° = 75°, so the case is SAS.

questions.question: From X to Y, the bearing is 300°. What is the back bearing from Y to X? Write a three-digit bearing.
questions.explanation: Since 300° + 180° is greater than 360°, subtract 180° instead: 300° - 180° = 120°.

questions.question: In one sentence, explain why a bearing of 060° points northeast rather than east.
questions.correctAnswer: A bearing is measured clockwise from north, and 060° is between north and east, so it points northeast.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that the reference direction is north, not east.

questions.question: A boat travels from A to B, then from B to C. Which segment usually represents the direct distance from the start to the final position?
questions.explanation: If the route is A to B to C, the direct distance from the start A to the final point C is AC.
